title: Capability Exposure Accounting for Threshold-Based Encrypted Backup Recovery: research artifact
description: Release 4.1.19 of the research artifact and manuscript for "Capability Exposure Accounting for Threshold-Based Encrypted Backup Recovery" (Samarjeet Malik, Shaurya Pratap Singh), the version the authors are submitting for publication to the International Journal of Information Security, approved by both authors. Since version 4.1.14 the manuscript has been revised in response to outside reviews; no theorem statement, proof or result changed. The changes: the abstract and introduction now present three primary contributions; the efficient-extraction remark after Theorem 14 is scoped; the complexity statements are exact (weakly NP-hard for weighted thresholds; NP-hard and APX-hard with reused credentials; XP in the number of generations, FPT open); the abstract states Theorem 14's hypotheses; the adaptivity wording is exact (transcript-adaptive observations); a deployment reading of the guessing factor L is added; the section references of the contributions are corrected; one reference year is corrected; the supplement Online Resource 1 names the journal. The artifact code (artifact/) is byte-identical to version 4.1.1 (10.5281/zenodo.24060229), which reproduces every result. On 10 Nov 2026 the archived v4.1.1 tag was re-run from a clean extract: all 99 tests and every TLC configuration pass, and all 13 plot-data files are byte-identical to the manuscript's (reproduction_logs_v4119/). A pinned container (Dockerfile) is built and run by a GitHub Actions workflow. The composition theorem (Theorem 24) is restricted-adaptive (guessing factor L), not fully adaptive, and an independent review of it is outstanding. No physical erasure, refinement proof or production readiness is claimed. Source: https://github.com/SamarjeetMalik/threshold-backup-capability-accounting (tag v4.1.19). Previous version: 10.5281/zenodo.24093096 (v4.1.14).
notes: Code and artifact (artifact/) under MIT; the manuscript, figures and plot data under CC BY 4.0. Springer class and style files keep their upstream terms.
